reason: The pancreatic cells are positioned to sense the higher glucose level after a meal.
expectation: The beta cells will respond to the glucose-rich blood by releasing insulin.

effect: The after-meal signal releases insulin into blood, with routes to both muscle and liver.
reaction: The two separate target branches make me curious about their different responses.
reason: The result shows insulin reaching skeletal muscle, making it a clear next target.
expectation: Insulin will promote glucose uptake by skeletal muscle.

alternatives.reason: The liver is the other target shown and may store glucose as glycogen.

effect: Insulin increased muscle glucose transport, and its release weakened as blood glucose fell. The liver is the other indicated target.
reaction: The feedback linking falling glucose to reduced insulin release is useful.
reason: The insulin signal also reaches the liver, which can store glucose as glycogen.
expectation: Insulin will promote glucose storage as glycogen in the liver.

effect: The liver stores glucose as glycogen and reduces glucose output after a meal; the after-meal goal is complete.
reaction: The distinction from muscle transporter insertion is useful.
reason: The pancreatic sensing cells can also respond to the lower glucose level between meals.
expectation: Alpha cells will release glucagon into the blood.

effect: Lower glucose prompted glucagon release, with its highlighted route reaching the liver.
reaction: The contrast with the after-meal insulin response is clear.
reason: Glucagon reaches the liver, where stored glycogen can help keep glucose available between meals.
expectation: Glucagon will promote glycogen breakdown and glucose release from the liver into blood.

effect: Glucagon promoted liver glycogen breakdown and glucose release; its stimulation diminished as blood glucose rose. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The return toward balance makes the between-meal feedback satisfying to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Comparing insulin’s effects on muscle and liver was most worthwhile: the planned pictures distinguish increased muscle glucose transport from liver glycogen storage and reduced glucose output.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial hormone-release combinations were fairly predictable from the labelled sensing cells and blood conditions, though they established the comparison.

surprise.text: The liver picture explicitly avoided a muscle-style transporter-insertion arrow, clarifying that the two target tissues respond differently.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; each followed a visible signal or target. The pictures did not explain how pancreatic cells sense glucose, however.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested in another chapter that connects contrasting organ responses with feedback, as this one did for insulin and glucagon.
